items.body:
COMPACT_MAGIC = "ptr-index/1c"

#: Hex characters of the body digest an index line shows in the compact form. The
#: line's digest is a *display* handle; the store re-hashes the full sha256 on read,
#: so shortening it cannot change which bytes a ref designates.
COMPACT_HASH_CHARS = 6

def _strip_revision(ref_text: str, revision: int) -> str:
    """Drop the ``@<revision>`` component of a serialized reference.

    The revision sits between the optional ``#pointer`` and the optional
    ``?projection`` (``@memory:m01@3?brief``), so it is not simply a suffix: the
    projection is split off first, then the revision, then the projection restored.
    """
    base, sep, projection = ref_text.partition("?")
    suffix = f"@{revision}"
    if base.endswith(suffix):
        base = base[: -len(suffix)]
    return base + sep + projection


def compact_index(index_text: str) -> CompactIndex:

def test_every_entry_round_trips_to_the_exact_original_bytes(index, scope, store, material):
    original = {(item["kind"], item["id"]): item["body"] for item in material}
    checked = 0
    for entry in index.entries.values():
        # The object is what resolves: this never re-reads the index text.
        ref = Reference(
            kind=entry.kind,
            id=entry.id,
            pointer=entry.pointer,
            revision=entry.ref.revision,
            projection=entry.projection,
        )
        target = resolve(ref, scope)
        body = store.get(target)
        assert hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest() == target.digest

        if entry.pointer is None:
            assert body.decode("utf-8") == original[(entry.kind, entry.id)]
        else:
            assert entry.size == len(body)
        checked += 1
    assert checked == len(material) == len(index.entries)


def test_pointer_entry_returns_the_selected_region(index, scope, store):
    target = resolve(parse("@artifact:plan#/goal@3"), scope)
    assert store.get(target) == b'"resolve lazily"'
